original_question: For each dimension n, does there exist a positive constant epsilon_n such that every open subset of R^n with volume at most epsilon_n admits an embedding into the unit ball that increases the lengths of all curves, equivalently a length-increasing embedding?
target_in_paper: Section 18, "Guth’s sponge": the paper asks whether, for each dimension n, there is a constant ε_n > 0 such that every open set U ⊂ R^n with volume at most ε_n admits a length-increasing embedding into a unit ball. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s target almost verbatim: it has the dimension-dependent constant ε_n, the class of domains (open subsets of R^n), the small-volume hypothesis, the target unit ball, and the existence of a length-increasing embedding. It also stays tightly scoped and does not broaden the problem beyond what Section 18 asks. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
missing_details: State explicitly that n is fixed and that the constant ε_n is allowed to depend on n. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
Specify that “volume” means n-dimensional Euclidean/Lebesgue measure on R^n; this is implicit in the paper’s ambient notation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
Specify that the target is the Euclidean unit n-ball B^n(1), since the paper only says “a unit ball.” ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))

If the question is to be fully stand-alone, define “length-increasing” explicitly: for every rectifiable curve γ in U, Length(f∘γ) ≥ Length(γ), using the Euclidean length structures on U and on the target ball. The paper uses the phrase but does not add a further nearby definition in Section 18. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
refined_question: For a fixed integer n ≥ 1, does there exist a constant ε_n > 0 such that every open set U ⊂ R^n with n-dimensional Lebesgue measure vol_n(U) ≤ ε_n admits an embedding f: U → B^n(1), where B^n(1) is the Euclidean unit n-ball, that is length-increasing with respect to the ambient Euclidean length structures; that is, Length(f∘γ) ≥ Length(γ) for every rectifiable curve γ in U? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
justification: This draft clearly targets Problem 18 rather than a neighboring topic. In this paper, Section 18 consists essentially of the problem statement itself plus the attribution to Larry Guth’s thesis, and the paper as a whole is presented as a gallery of open problems rather than a theorem–proposition development. So the paper-faithful refinement is simply to preserve the exact quantifier structure and make the implicit Euclidean and metric-measure conventions explicit, without adding any extra hypotheses or generalizations. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
